findings.title: Image user should not be 'root'
findings.evidence: Specify at least 1 USER command in Dockerfile with non-root user as argument
findings.explanation: Running containers with 'root' user can lead to a container escape situation. It is a best practice to run containers as non-root users, which can be done by adding a 'USER' statement to the Dockerfile. Specify at least 1 USER command in Dockerfile with non-root user as argument
findings.impact: Insecure infrastructure configuration widens the attack surface or the blast radius of a compromise.
findings.remediation: Add 'USER <non root user name>' line to the Dockerfile

findings.title: `POST /private/users` changes state with no visible authentication
findings.explanation: This is a heuristic. Neither the handler (lines 23-38) nor its file shows a recognisable authentication or authorization check (e.g. `Depends(get_current_user)`, `@login_required`, `getServerSession`, `requireAuth`). The app may still enforce auth elsewhere: global middleware, an API gateway, or router-level dependencies registered in another file.
findings.impact: If no auth is enforced anywhere, anyone who can reach the server can create, modify or delete data through this endpoint.
findings.remediation: Confirm where authentication is enforced. If it is not, add an auth dependency/middleware to this route and check that the caller may act on the specific resource (not just that they are logged in).
